title: Add integration tests for tampering, replay/downgrade, and time-skew in offline bundle verification
creator: Ethan Park
description:
Background
Offline bundle signing is a hard security boundary for Redwood Private in air-gapped environments. We need confidence that the installer fails closed across a realistic set of attacker and operator error scenarios (tampered artifacts, replay/downgrade attempts, and time skew).

This ticket adds integration tests that exercise the end-to-end verification flow in the on-prem installer preflight path using real bundle layouts (manifest + detached signature) and common failure modes observed in pilots.

Goals
- Ensure we fail closed (block install/upgrade) on:
  - Modified manifest contents after signing
  - Swapped or corrupted artifacts where hash mismatch is detected
  - Truncated/partial bundles
  - Replay of an older valid signature/manifest (downgrade attempt)
  - Known time-skew scenarios (not-yet-valid and expired)
- Ensure tests cover the UX contract:
  - Stable error codes/reasons for Support triage
  - Log locations and remediation hints are printed
  - Break-glass behavior (when enabled) is explicitly logged and marked

Non-goals
- Full cryptographic validation of underlying libraries (assume libsodium/openssl primitives are correct).
- Performance benchmarking of verification (separate SRE/release pipeline work).

Proposed approach
1) Test harness
- Add an integration test suite that runs the installer in a containerized environment with a temp directory representing an extracted bundle.
- Use a fixture generator to build a minimal offline bundle layout:
  - bundle/manifest.json (canonical)
  - bundle/manifest.sig (detached)
  - bundle/artifacts/... (small placeholder files)
  - bundle/sbom/... (if present; can be optional in fixtures)
- Keep fixture generation deterministic; do not rely on network.

2) Tamper/corruption test cases
- Tamper: modify a single byte in manifest.json after signing -> verify fails with SIG_INVALID (or equivalent).
- Hash mismatch: keep manifest and signature intact, but modify one artifact file -> verify fails with ARTIFACT_HASH_MISMATCH and names the path that failed.
- Truncated: delete one required artifact referenced in manifest -> verify fails with ARTIFACT_MISSING.
- Swapped artifact: replace artifact with different file of same name -> verify fails with ARTIFACT_HASH_MISMATCH.

3) Replay/downgrade test cases
- Simulate installed state record showing current version/build-id.
- Provide a valid, signed bundle with a lower version/build-id:
  - expected: preflight fails with DOWNGRADE_BLOCKED and prints both versions.
- Provide a valid bundle with same version but different build-id:
  - expected: defined behavior should be consistent with downgrade policy (block if build-id decreases or if policy is strict). Align with ENG-4823/PR behavior.

4) Time-skew test cases
We have customers with poor/absent NTP in air-gapped networks.
- Not-yet-valid: create a signature/cert validity window in the future relative to the test runner time OR use installer time override flag if implemented.
  - expected: verify fails with SIGNATURE_NOT_YET_VALID and prints local clock + guidance.
- Expired: same but with past validity.
  - expected: verify fails with SIGNATURE_EXPIRED.
Notes:
- If implementation is using key-based signatures without X.509 validity (e.g., ed25519 detached signature only), time-skew must be tested against the installer’s “signature validity window” metadata (if present) or against the trust root metadata (key activation dates). If no time component exists in the signature scheme, keep time-skew tests focused on installer logic that currently checks “not before” (per PR-24961 work).

5) CI integration
- Run integration suite in CI for redwood-private-installer on PRs touching verification/bundles.
- Ensure suite runtime stays under ~5 minutes; use cached build artifacts for the installer binary where possible.
- Add a single “golden path” success test to ensure fixtures aren’t only negative.

Acceptance criteria
- Integration test suite added and running in CI (required check) for redwood-private-installer.
- Minimum test coverage includes:
  - manifest modified after signing
  - referenced artifact modified after signing
  - referenced artifact missing
  - truncated bundle (simulated by missing signature or manifest)
  - downgrade blocked when installed version > bundle version
  - at least one time-skew related failure mode (not-yet-valid or expired) consistent with current signature envelope behavior
- Tests assert on:
  - installer exit code
  - error code (or normalized reason) emitted
  - presence of log path / remediation hint
- Documentation in the repo for how to run the suite locally.

Implementation notes / constraints
- Prefer black-box testing the installer CLI (preflight) rather than calling verification functions directly, to catch wiring errors (flags, trust store loading, state record path).
- Keep test fixtures very small (KB/MB order) to avoid repo bloat.
- Ensure tests do not print secrets; redact any embedded keys used for test signing. Use dedicated test keys only.

Relevant links
- Confluence (design): offline-signing-and-verification-design
- Confluence (threat model): threat-model-offline-bundle-signing
- GitHub PR targets:
  - redwood-private-installer PR-24995 (integration tests for tampered bundles)
  - redwood-private-installer PR-24902 (downgrade prevention)
  - redwood-private-installer PR-24961 (time skew guidance)

Rollout / risk
- Blocking failures in CI may slow down verification feature iteration; mitigate via keeping fixture generation fast and using focused test matrix.
- Ensure failures are deterministic (no reliance on wall clock beyond explicit time override tests).

Owner notes
- Devon to implement; Ethan to review verification-specific assertions; Marcus Lin to sanity check security-relevant test cases and naming of failure reasons.
comments: 2025-11-01 (Devon Price): Started a draft harness that shells out to `redwood-private-installer preflight --offline-bundle <path> --verify-only`. I’m keeping the fixture generator in test code so we don’t commit large tarballs.

2025-11-06 (Ethan Park): Please assert on the normalized error reason, not raw stderr text. Support wants stable codes (hash mismatch vs signature invalid vs unknown key). Coordinate with ENG-4823 taxonomy.

2025-11-12 (Marcus Lin): Add at least one test that validates we fail closed when signature file is missing (manifest present but no .sig). This is a common “partial transfer” scenario and should not degrade to unsigned install.

2025-11-18 (Devon Price): Added negative cases for: modified manifest, modified artifact, missing artifact, missing signature. All fail closed. Working on downgrade replay tests next; blocked on final state-record path constant from PR-24902.

2025-12-02 (Jordan Lee): Canonicalization note: for the tampered-manifest test, ensure the tamper is post-canonicalization (edit a value) rather than reformatting JSON spacing, since spacing differences should already be normalized by canonicalization.

2025-12-09 (Devon Price): Downgrade tests added using a temp install state file (current_version=2026.01.0, bundle_version=2025.12.3). Preflight returns DOWNGRADE_BLOCKED. Also added same-version different build-id case; currently allowed if version equal. If we change policy later, update expected result.
2025-12-15 (Sahana Iyer): CI runtime concern: the suite is ~7m on cold cache. Suggest building installer once, then reusing binary across test cases (table-driven) rather than rebuilding per case.

2026-01-08 (Devon Price): Time-skew coverage: added `--time-override` test path from PR-24961; when set to a time before key activation date, verification fails SIGNATURE_NOT_YET_VALID with remediation hint. Also added a golden-path success test.
2026-01-17 (Ethan Park): Merged via PR-24995. CI check now required for verification-related changes. Marking ticket Done.
